The certificate submodule shall maintain the status of a certificate and provide the status on demand.

A certificate has the status KEYM_CERTIFICATE_VALID if it was parsed and verified completely against other certificates of the PKI. All certificates of the chain of trust are available and verified completely.

Elements of the certificate associated and defined in KeyMCertificateElement and subcontainers shall be used to verify elements of the certificate according to the configuration. This shall be done for every certificate that has to be verified.

A certificate is in the status KEYM_CERTIFICATE_INVALID if the contents could not be parsed due to an internal error, e.g. a format error, signature failure period failure or any other failure occurred during the verification.

A certificate has the status KEYM_CERTIFICATE_PARSED_NOT_VALIDATED if the certificate has been provided e.g. with the function KeyM_SetCertificate() and has been parsed successfully, but the verification has not yet been initiated, e.g. by a call to KeyM_VerifyCertificate().
A certificate has the status KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_PARSED if the certificate was already provided, e.g. with KeyM_SetCertificate() but the parsing process is still ongoing in the background.
If a certificate shall be verified but has not yet been parsed, the parsing operation shall be done as soon as possible and the verification process shall be started afterwards.

A certificate is in the status KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_AVAILABLE if the certificate has not yet been provided by a function call KeyM_SetCertificate() or the function was called with the certificate ID but with certificate length of 0.

The status of a certificate can be reset by calling KeyM_SetCertificate() with the corresponding certificate ID but with length information 0. The function will return E_OK and will reset the status of the certificate to KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_AVAILABLE (see KeyM_CertGetStatus()).

Reporting verification of a certificate chain failed: In case the verification of a certificate against a certificate chain, that has been provided temporarily for this purpose was not successful, KeyM shall raise SEV_CERT_ CHAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED to the IdsM.

Reporting initial persistent certificate installation: Upon completion of the initial installation attempt of a persistent certificate, whether it was successful or unsuccessful, KeyM shall raise SEV_CERT_INSTALL to the IdsM.

Reporting update of a persistent certificate: Upon completion of the update attempt of a persistent certificate, whether it was successful or unsuccessful, KeyM shall raise SEV_CERT_UPDATE to the IdsM.

Reporting removal of a persistent certificate: Upon completion of the removal attempt of a persistent certificate, whether it was successful or unsuccessful, KeyM shall raise SEV_CERT_DELETE to the IdsM.
Reporting invalid installed certificate: In case an already installed persistent certificate is detected as invalid, KeyM shall raise SEV_CERT_INSTALLED_BUT_INVALID to the IdsM.

The AUTOSAR LdCom module’s initialization function LdCom_Init shall initialize all internal data.
The AUTOSAR LdCom module shall provide the API function LdCom_DeInit for de-initialization of the AUTOSAR LdCom module. Inside this function call all de-initialization shall take place.
When LdCom_Transmit is invoked, LdCom shall invoke PduR_LdComTransmit by replacing the Signal Id by the according PDU Id.
LdCom shall pass invocations of LdCom_Transmit to PduR_LdComTransmit by replacing the Signal Id by the according PDU Id.
The API LdCom_GetVersionInfo shall be configured byLdComVersionInfoAPI.
LdCom_TriggerTransmit shall only be available if at least one LdComIPdu has LdComTxTriggerTransmit configured.
LdCom_CopyTxData, LdCom_TpTxConfirmation shall only be available if at least one LdComIPdu has LdComIPduDirection configured to LDCOM_SEND and LdComApiType configured to LDCOM_TP.

LdCom_StartOfReception, LdCom_CopyRxData, LdCom_TpRxIndicationshall only be available if at least one LdComIPdu has LdComIPduDirection configured to LDCOM_RECEIVE and LdComApiType configured to LDCOM_TP.
The LdCom implementation shall include Det.h if LdComDevErrorDetect is enabled.
